long_biography.plain_text:
Multiplayer responsiveness became one of Yahn W. Bernier's defining technical problems at Valve. His work on Half-Life's network code addressed the tension between immediate player feedback and the delays inherent in online play. He later set out the resulting latency-compensation methods in a technical paper for game developers.

Bernier's contribution extended beyond one title. He served as a development lead for Team Fortress 2, worked on Half-Life 2 and participated in the creation of Steam. His credits span much of Valve's catalogue, reflecting a career built around the systems and tools underlying both games and distribution.
